Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

Each draft's own explanation

To both parties: the rider's claim is upheld, and the SGD 4.50 no-show fee is refunded in full. What the record shows. The driver accepted the trip at 20:22:12 on 17 Aug, pressed 'arrived' at 20:28:14 and cancelled at 20:32:36 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW (EV-TRIP-02711). The platform charged the rider SGD 4.50 (EV-FARE-02711: total_charged 4.50, cancellation_fee 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). Arrival fails. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02711, weight 1.0, COMPLETE, 69 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0) places the driver's closest approach to the pickup pin at 156.99 m anywhere in the trip, with 0 fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and 0 continuous in-geofence runs. POL-NS-02's proximity test therefore fails, and with it POL-NS-01 limb (b): the driver did not arrive at the pickup point. POL-NS-12 does not help the driver - arrival_marker is BUTTON, not GPS_AUTO, so a pressed marker stays subject to POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-05, and the bare statement that he 'was at the pickup as shown on the map' is corroborated by no telemetry. Dwell fails independently. The free waiting period in force is 180 s (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec). The effective in-geofence dwell is 0 s, measured - per POL-NS-01(c) - from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and not from the 'arrived' tap. POL-NS-06 therefore makes the fee not chargeable on a 180 s shortfall, with no driver compensation, and POL-NS-01 limb (d) cannot be met either because the dwell never elapsed.
